name: Renal Dysplasia, Unilateral

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiologic Diagnostic Criteria for Unilateral Renal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Ultrasound or MRI showing unilateral renal hypoplasia or multicystic dysplastic kidney
Absent or severely reduced function of the affected kidney on nuclear renal scan
Normal morphology and function of contralateral kidney
Exclusion of obstructive uropathy or other structural anomalies causing secondary dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging evidence of unilateral renal dysplasia plus absent or severely reduced function of the affected kidney, with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiologic supported by functional studies; biopsy rarely required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral renal hypoplasia with multicystic dysplastic kidney
searchTerms: small kidney with cysts on one side
unilateral renal hypoplasia with cystic kidney
underdeveloped kidney with cysts on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or severely reduced function of one kidney
searchTerms: one kidney not working or missing
absent or severely reduced kidney function
loss of function in one kidney

common.symptomName: Asymptomatic abdominal mass detected on imaging
Mild hypertension secondary to reduced renal mass
searchTerms: mild high blood pressure from reduced kidney size
hypertension due to smaller kidney mass
slightly elevated blood pressure from kidney loss

occasional.symptomName: Mild abdominal discomfort or flank pain
Growth retardation due to chronic kidney disease progression
searchTerms: poor growth due to kidney problems
growth delay from chronic kidney issues

rare.symptomName: Progression to chronic kidney disease stage 3 or higher
searchTerms: moderate to severe chronic kidney disease
kidney problems on the other side

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated serum creatinine depending on contralateral kidney function
Urinalysis may show proteinuria or hematuria
Nuclear renal scan showing absent or severely reduced function in affected kidney
imaging: Ultrasound demonstrating unilateral small, cystic, or hypoplastic kidney
MRI or CT confirming dysplastic changes and absence of normal renal architecture
Nuclear medicine renal scintigraphy showing functional deficit
other: Physical exam may reveal palpable abdominal mass in infants
Blood pressure monitoring for early detection of hypertension

distinguishingFeatures: Bilateral involvement leading to renal failure
Presence of urinary tract obstruction on imaging

redFlags: Severe hypertension in infancy or early childhood
